parameter_matrix.note: Synchronous rectification eliminates external Schottky diode loss and PCB area.
Compact WSON/VSON/SOT-563 packages demand tight hot-loop layout and thermal vias.
A part wins only if its operating Vin range strictly encompasses the counterpart on both ends.
Provides transient overshoot margin above nominal DC supply bus.
Fixed-output variants save divider BOM; adjustable parts allow arbitrary rail tuning up to switch BVdss limits.
For boost/switch-limited converters, usable Iout ≈ Isw × (Vin / Vout) × η minus half ripple ΔIL/2.
Dominates light-load efficiency and standby battery runtime.
Higher fsw shrinks inductor footprint; lower fsw reduces switching losses & high-band EMI.
Check datasheet efficiency curve at your exact Vin/Vout/Iout operating point.
Ensure inductor Isat exceeds worst-case peak switch current by >= 20–30%.
Any Vref discrepancy requires recalculating feedback divider R1/R2.
Lower θJA improves continuous load thermal headroom on compact 2-layer PCBs.

swap_risks: CRITICAL SWITCH-VOLTAGE OVERSTRESS RISK: LM27313XMF/NOPB is rated up to only 28 V output (p.1) vs LM2733XMF/NOPB up to 38 V (p.3); exceeding the internal switch BVdss ceiling destroys the SW MOSFET.

CAUTION CURRENT RATING BASIS: LM27313XMF/NOPB specifies 800 mA (switch current limit Isw, p.5) vs LM2733XMF/NOPB 1000 mA (switch current limit Isw, p.4). Remember boost/switch-limited Iout,max is strictly less than Isw due to duty-cycle and inductor ripple scaling.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 26% higher on LM2733XMF/NOPB (LM27313XMF/NOPB: 166.3 °C/W p.4 vs LM2733XMF/NOPB: 210 °C/W p.4); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
engineering_verdict: LM27313XMF/NOPB (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) and LM2733XMF/NOPB (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because adjustable Vout,max ceiling drops >=20% (28 V vs 38 V — switch-voltage overstress risk); current rating or switch-limit basis differs; θJA worsens 26% (thermal derating verification required). Power-stage deltas: boost (non-sync) vs boost (non-sync), switching frequency 1600 kHz (p.5) vs 1600 kHz (p.5) (1x ratio), typical inductor 10 µH (p.1) vs 10 µH (p.1), feedback Vref 1.23 V (p.5) vs 1.23 V (p.4), and package θJA 166.3 vs 210 °C/W. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM27313XMF/NOPB "Feedforward Capacitor Cf Across R1 Is Mandatory for Loop Stability" (p.11) and LM2733XMF/NOPB "Mandatory Feedforward Capacitor Cf Across R1 Prevents Loop Oscillation" (p.13). BOM decision: Choose LM27313XMF/NOPB when matching your existing Texas Instruments SOT-23-5 (DBV) qualification and -40..125 °C grade; choose LM2733XMF/NOPB when higher switch current capacity (1000 mA) is required or programmed output rails exceed 28 V (up to 38 V). Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
